name: SHELF FREQUENCY: The Open Broadcast
subcategory: community pirate radio and neural feed
creator: Collective origin — attributed to 'the Tendaji-Rocha cell,' Shelf District 7
description: A decentralized pirate broadcast network operating across the Shelf since 2197, Shelf Frequency transmits on rotating legacy radio bands, low-power neural bleed channels, and improvised mesh-relay nodes stitched together from salvaged BCI hardware. Programming is unscheduled and community-sourced: grief announcements, missing-person calls, neighborhood dispute mediation, music, oral poetry, and emergency information during blackouts. There is no editorial board — content is authenticated by a rotating council of neighborhood proxies who change identity weekly to avoid corporate enforcement.
medium: legacy audio (primary), low-power neural bleed, mesh relay
cultural_impact: Shelf Frequency is the only broadcast infrastructure that reliably reaches Tier 1 during corponation-imposed communication blackouts; it has become the de facto emergency information system for communities that official networks treat as expendable.
controversy: HelixCorp's Compliance Division has attempted to shut down Shelf Frequency seventeen documented times; each shutdown has been followed within days by a reconstituted broadcast under a new node cluster. Two alleged founders were arrested in 2214 under the Unauthorized Spectrum Act.
story_hooks: The rotating council's authentication system has been compromised — someone is broadcasting false emergency instructions through Shelf Frequency during a crisis, and no one knows if the real council has been captured or has gone dark voluntarily.
A Tier 4 journalist wants to embed with Shelf Frequency to document its operation, but the council is split on whether the exposure would protect them or mark them for final shutdown.

Shelf Frequency intercepts a fragment of encrypted corporate communication suggesting a planned infrastructure demolition in District 7 — but broadcasting it could reveal how they obtained the signal.
